clue.text: Pack things

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, to cram or fill tightly
second meaning: a noun, miscellaneous belongings or items

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one instruction it sounds like packing a suitcase; the two words are separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb meaning cram full and as an informal noun for assorted possessions.

clue.text: Plate I ate, no mixed grill ultimately

indicators.note: things that are mixed are jumbled together, so the preceding letters are rearranged
ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the neighbouring word is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of grill

explanation.surface: Someone finished their plate but refused the mixed grill at the end of the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plate' and 'mixed grill' set a dinner scene, but the plate is the anatomical kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail is a hard horny plate growing on a digit, so the one on a foot is such a plate.

clue.text: Added extras — in the hairdressing salon?

blocks.note: surface reading: perks an employee gets on top of salary
setter's reading: a fringe is hair cut across the forehead, so in a salon the perks might literally be fringes

explanation.walkthrough: A fringe is the hair cut short across the forehead; the question mark flags the punning second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: These are perks such as a company car or health insurance given in addition to wages.

clue.text: Sweet, country's borders?

indicators.note: the borders of something are its edges, so only the outermost letters of the word are wanted

blocks.note: the first and last letters of country

explanation.surface: A query about whether a nation's frontiers are pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: The borders of country are C and Y, and saying that out as 'C and Y' spells the answer; the question mark admits the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Candy is the American word for confectionery, any sweet.

clue.text: Missing round hard receptacle designed for powdery residue

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: something missing has gone astray
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A sturdy container for powder has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The powdery residue is cigarette ash, which the long definition describes coyly.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a dish made for smokers to tap cigarette ash into, ash being a powdery residue.

clue.text: Extraordinary tiredness in person expressing resistance

indicators.note: something extraordinary is out of its normal form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone protesting is suffering from remarkable fatigue.
explanation.definitionFit: One who dissents disagrees openly with authority, a form of objection or opposition.

clue.text: European eaten by wolf in Newfoundland

indicators.note: something eaten by other words sits inside them, so the answer lies within the following letters

blocks.note: found across wolf, in and Newfoundland

explanation.surface: A traveller from Europe is devoured by a wolf in eastern Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Finland, a Nordic country, is a European.

clue.text: Lentils and meats in different food processor

indicators.note: making something different changes its form, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget is being used to blend pulses and meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Food processor' suggests a kitchen blender, but the definition is the part of the gut that digests food.
explanation.definitionFit: This part of the digestive tract breaks down and absorbs nutrients, so it literally processes food.

clue.text: Ring number of US soldiers up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: ten is a number
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: An order to summon a group of American troops to stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring number' suggests a phone call; Ring is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A signet is a finger ring bearing a seal or monogram.

clue.text: Unspeakable wickedness in beauty

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

blocks.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
evil is wickedness

explanation.surface: Indescribable sin hidden within a lovely person.
explanation.walkthrough: A dish is informal British slang for a good-looking person.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something dreadfully bad, so awful it can hardly be spoken of.

clue.text: Top clubs, say, welcoming twin males?

indicators.note: welcoming someone takes them in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: clubs is an example of a suit in cards
two of M, the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: Top nightclubs are welcoming a pair of twin brothers.
explanation.definitionFit: A summit is the highest point of a hill, synonymous with its peak.

clue.text: Poison drink? That's the limit!

blocks.note: to mar is to spoil or poison
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: An outraged cry at someone poisoning a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A margin is an edge or border, the boundary line or limit of something.

clue.text: White lies disseminated in gang

indicators.note: disseminated means scattered about, so those letters are spread into a new order
in places one group of letters inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
a ring is a gang of criminals

explanation.surface: Harmless falsehoods spread around inside a criminal gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White lies' reads as one phrase; White alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Riesling is a grape and the white wine made from it.

clue.text: Track alongside sign in quiet location?

blocks.note: Libra is a sign of the zodiac
RY is an abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: Running alongside a signpost at a silent spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alongside' only places the track piece next to the sign piece, after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Silence is traditionally required in a library, so it is a place for quiet; the question mark marks it as a definition by example.

clue.text: Sauna made to break down again and again and again!

indicators.note: something broken down falls apart, so the letters reassemble in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sauna keeps breaking down over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: The repetitive definition itself mimics something done to the point of tedium.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'to sickness', the phrase means repeated so often that it becomes tiresome.

clue.text: A number dry, waters finally drained out

indicators.note: what is drained out is removed, so a letter is taken away
finally points to the end, so just the final letter of the word is meant

blocks.note: thirsty means dry
the last letter of waters

explanation.surface: A count of dried-up wells whose water has run out.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirty is the cardinal three times ten, so it is a number.

clue.text: Rule about new gun

indicators.note: about means around, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: a canon is a rule or law
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A regulation concerning a newly issued firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannon is a large heavy artillery gun.

clue.text: A teacher is someone beautiful

blocks.note: taken as written
a don is a university teacher
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tribute to a handsome teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a lecturer at Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis was the youth of Greek myth loved by Aphrodite, and the name now means any handsome young man.

clue.text: Good prices for freebooters

blocks.note: PI, short for pious, means good
rates are prices

explanation.surface: Fair charges for plunderers.
explanation.walkthrough: PI for pious is a crossword convention for good.
explanation.definitionFit: Freebooters are sea robbers who plunder ships for loot.

clue.text: Initially, prose saying further unnecessary bits

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: the first letter of prose
adding means saying further, as in 'he added'

explanation.surface: A writer's prose says more than it needs to, with superfluous parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Padding is superfluous material inserted into writing or speech to make it longer.

clue.text: Drug otherwise used in eating regimens rejected

indicators.note: something used in a thing is put inside it, so one piece enters the other
rejected means sent back, so the letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: diets are eating regimens
or means otherwise

explanation.surface: A drug that might be taken on a diet is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' looks like a container signal, but it belongs with regimens as the diets.
explanation.definitionFit: Steroids are a class of drugs, including hormones misused by athletes.

clue.text: Puzzle scam uncovered

blocks.note: a con is a scam
something uncovered has been found

explanation.surface: A baffling fraud has been exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: To confound is to bewilder or perplex someone, as a puzzle does.

clue.text: Ruined, as are three-wheelers and go-karts?

blocks.note: first meaning: wrecked, as hopes are
second meaning: both these words are written with a hyphen, a short line

explanation.walkthrough: The vehicles suggest crashes, but the point is how the words are written: each contains a hyphen.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopes that are dashed are destroyed, and hyphenated words are written with dashes.

clue.text: Secure nothing in political party

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A party fails to win any seats.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is a unionist party in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten up buttons or a coat is to make it secure.

clue.text: Walk quietly — possible instruction to reader in formal attire

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a tie is part of formal attire, as in black tie
PTO, please turn over, is printed at the foot of a page for the reader

explanation.surface: A reader in evening dress is told to move silently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black tie' on an invitation means formal dress, so tie stands for formal attire.
explanation.definitionFit: To tiptoe is to walk on the balls of the feet so as to make no noise.

clue.text: Small parts married together

indicators.note: a thing that parts a phrase splits it open by sitting inside it

blocks.note: a married couple are in union
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Pieces of something tiny are joined together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small parts' looks like a noun phrase, but parts is the verb doing the splitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in unison means acting simultaneously and in agreement, all together.

clue.text: Picture, for example, Parisian pal sent back

indicators.note: sent back means returned the way it came, so the letters read the opposite way

blocks.note: e.g. abbreviates for example
ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: A photo of a French friend, for instance, being posted home.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture or likeness of something.

clue.text: United team is ahead, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word is judged on how it is heard, not spelled

blocks.note: a team that is ahead leads

explanation.surface: A football fan reports their team is winning.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds United is an English football club, so the city stands for the team.
explanation.definitionFit: The club's full name is Leeds United, so the city's name identifies that United football team.
